title: BDK06 8-round AES-192 / aes192-8r-related-key-id-3-columns-bdk2006

target.description: Shifted AES-192 interval, original rounds 2–9, with the preceding subkey and no final MixColumns. Explicit output is 168 mixed boundary-subkey bits, not a separately completed 192-bit master key. It guesses 3 last-round columns plus one preceding subkey byte and filters the eight-byte earlier subkey list; the output width changes with g.

setting.key_relation: Two structures of16 secret AES-192 keys each, inducing256 cross pairs. Across a pair the master-key XOR has DeltaK[3]=f and DeltaK[8]=DeltaK[12]=DeltaK[16]=DeltaK[20]=a, other bytes0. The attacker chooses nonzero a; f is varied by the structures, while b,c and for8r d are actual nonlinear schedule differences, handled as in Sections3.3/4.2.
setting.plaintext_model: Aggregate related-key chosen-plaintext queries under thirty-two structured keys; Section 3.3 gives 2^52 plaintext identities each under sixteen keys, while Section 4 gives per-key pools.
assumptions: Section 3.3 estimates 0.63 probability that the key structures contain a suitable pair. This is not automatically a numerical complete-key success probability.
Output widths count named selected-subkey values, not proved independent master-key bits. The remaining key-recovery completion is not priced.
This endpoint recovers 168 named subkey bits; other widths are not equivalent recovery goals.
The source conversion 2^6 memory accesses per encryption equivalent is an accounting convention, not a calibrated implementation measurement.
ZWZF07 Section5.1 identifies an error in all three BDK06 eight-round extensions; preserve these historical quotations with an explicit source conflict.

success.description: No valid numerical recovery success is established for this historical eight-round endpoint. ZWZF07 Section5.1 already contradicts the backward-extension filter; retain that published correction and the original resource quotations. The original2^-120 is a conditional wrong-list bound under one terminal guess;2^-16 is an expected full suggestion count, neither an independently valid recovery rate. The32-key suitable-pair model is not success of the disputed168/136/104-bit output.

components.description: Section4.1 source fraction of pairs satisfying zero difference in 1 unguessed terminal columns. Historical filter quantity only: the existing ZWZF07 backward-extension correction invalidates using this as a valid complete attack.

Section4.2 historical source bound for some wrong64-bit whitening guess remaining under ONE fixed104-bit terminal guess after2^71 pairs. The source then multiplies by2^104 to obtain expected suggestion count about2^-16. This model does not repair the independently documented invalid backward extension.

Section3.3: two16-key structures induce256 cross pairs. This is the source approximately independent/uniform256-trial model for at least one suitable subkey-difference pair. Pair dependence is not independently proved, and this event does not quantify candidate uniqueness or output recovery.

review.scope: Re-read BDK06 PDF4-12 and ZWZF07 PDF7-9 Section5.1. The published backward-extension correction affects all three column variants and the known-differences internal core. Withdraw the raw-first proposed Markov recovery bounds: their true-candidate-retention premise fails for the historical zero filter. Preserve all author components, original costs and correction conflicts; primary remains unquantified.

field_conflicts.label: published-eight-round-backward-extension-error
field_conflicts.description: ZWZF07 Section5.1 identifies an error in all three BDK06 eight-round extensions. In the detailed first variant, the zero-difference filter in the unguessed terminal column forces a nonzero input8 byte4 after the equivalent-key addition, contradicting the zero value required by the impossible core. Historical cost quotations remain unchanged; they are not established valid attack costs.

observations.locator: PDF pp.10–12 / printed pp.30–32, Sections4.1–4.2, especially the zero filter in bytes1,4,11,14 and subsequent impossible-core test.
observations.reported: First variant guesses12 bytes of k9 plus w8[11], treats zero difference in the other four terminal bytes, and quotes T=2^184, D=2^68.5; other variants quote T=2^159/D=2^92 and T=2^134/D=2^116.

observations.locator: PDF pp.7–9 / printed pp.21–23, Section5.1 and Figure1.
observations.reported: For the first BDK06 variant, zero terminal column1 implies nonzero Delta x8^I[4] because MC^-1(Delta k8 Col1) has a nonzero byte4, whereas the core requires Delta x8^I[4]=0. Section5.1 states similar errors for the second and third variants.
